summary: IDR Gateway Now Available The new Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) Gateway improves functionality, security, and efficiency of the Federal IDR process On November 13, 2026, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Labor, and the Department of the Treasury (the Departments) launched the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) Gateway, a new platform for group health plans, health insurance issuers, providers, facilities, and providers of air ambulance services (collectively referred to as “parties”) and their representatives to manage disputes under the Federal IDR process. The IDR Gateway provides a secure, centralized system that streamlines the dispute lifecycle, allowing users to submit, track, and manage payment disputes from start to finish. Managing Disputes Throughout the IDR Lifecycle The IDR Gateway is a single platform for managing payment disputes from start to finish. In the IDR Gateway, parties and their representatives can start a dispute using the “Notice of IDR Initiation” feature, respond to certified IDR entity selections by completing the “IDR Entity Selection Response” and “IDR Entity Reselection Response” feature, and submit payment offers by completing the “Notice of Offer” feature. IDR Gateway users can also view reports and access dispute records for all open and some closed disputes associated with their organization. Moreover, the IDR Gateway allows parties and their representatives to track disputes by phase and identify critical upcoming dispute deadlines. Tools available to IDR Gateway users include: IDR Gateway Dashboard: The IDR Gateway Dashboard is available to users who have joined an organization. It provides a visual snapshot of disputes associated with an organization by displaying color-coded information on dispute phases for open disputes. Phases can help organizations determine the current status or next actions on a dispute. Each color-coded section displays the total number of disputes in the IDR Entity Selection, IDR Entity Eligibility Review, Offer Submission, and IDR Entity Offer Review phases of the Federal IDR process. Search: The search function allows IDR Gateway users who have joined an organization to find disputes using dispute numbers or keywords. This function also provides filters to narrow search results by date range, dispute status or phase, or disputes with selection or offers due. Reports: Users who have joined an organization can view and filter a wide range of data associated with the organization’s disputes by generating specific reports to better monitor and analyze IDR processes and outcomes. Specifically, users can generate detailed reports of: open and closed disputes; open dispute line items; closed dispute line items; resubmission requested line items; disputes with selection due; and disputes with offers due. Notifications: System notifications provide important updates or actions related to a user’s account or disputes. Users can view a summary of recent system notifications, as well as manage, archive, filter, and review notifications by specific notification types (active, by dispute, by user, by organization, and archived). New tools and features that further enhance disputing party access and experience – such as the IDR Registry – will be added in the future on a rolling basis. Enhanced Security The IDR Gateway provides important new security features to protect the integrity of the Federal IDR process. Specifically, the IDR Gateway includes new identity verification processes and protocols that permit only U.S.-based users to access the Federal IDR process. All IDR Gateway users must verify their identity with an approved credential service provider during the account creation process. Individuals who do not verify their identity cannot access the IDR Gateway, helping to prevent fraud and unauthorized access. In addition to identity verification, the IDR Gateway will require users to agree to terms and conditions for responsible and secure usage of the IDR Gateway. The agreements signed by users include notice that unauthorized users may be subject to criminal prosecution, administrative actions or other adverse actions as needed. The Future of Web Forms Outside the IDR Gateway The IDR Gateway is replacing the single-use web forms that parties currently use to manage disputes. For a limited period, parties may continue to submit web forms without signing in to the IDR Gateway. The web forms will no longer be available outside the IDR Gateway after January 15, 2027 (with the exception of the “Notice of IDR Initiation – Resubmission” web form, which will remain available until that functionality is ended as finalized in the Federal IDR Operations final rule.) ### CMS News and Media Group Catherine Howden, Director Media Inquiries Form 202-690-6145
